sections.title: Course information
sections.text: PHC 6149 Public Health Leadership. Online, Spring 2026. [INSTRUCTOR] [EMAIL_1]

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.text: Students will apply leadership theories to public health organizations and communicate a shared vision to stakeholders.

sections.title: Week 3: Leading change
sections.text: Readings on change management. Discussion post (ungraded).

sections.title: Week 6: Negotiation and collaboration
sections.text: Negotiation role-play with a partner from another discipline (ungraded).

sections.title: Leadership reflection paper
sections.text: A 5-page reflection paper applying one leadership theory to a public health case. 25% of the grade.

sections.title: Final project: vision statement
sections.text: Teams draft and present a vision statement for a local health department. 35% of the grade.

sections.title: Course policies
sections.text: Late work loses 10% per day. Academic integrity policy applies.

reasons: The syllabus has no AI policy (section: policies).
No assignment uses or discusses AI tools.

edits.proposed: AI use policy: AI tools are allowed for brainstorming and editing only. Disclose any AI use in a short note at the end of each submission.
edits.rationale: The syllabus has no AI policy. A stated, restricted-use policy gives students clear expectations and matches the school's disclosure rule.

evidence.title: ASPPH AI Framework
evidence.snippet: Faculty should be able to clearly define acceptable use, whether through complete prohibition, restricted use, or transparent collaborative use.

edits.original: Negotiation role-play with a partner from another discipline (ungraded).
edits.proposed: Graded interprofessional negotiation simulation (10%): teams of public health and nursing students negotiate a shared response plan, using an AI-generated stakeholder brief they must fact-check. Submit the plan plus a 1-page reflection on where the AI brief was wrong or incomplete.
edits.rationale: Making the role-play an assessed simulation gives assessed evidence for competency 21, and the reflection teaches the limits of AI tools.
